QF.id: III-C Prevention of Money Laundering Act_23

question.text: The written Anti-Money Laundering procedures adopted by a registered intermediary must include which of the following parameters?

answer.text: All four: policy for acceptance of clients; procedure for identifying clients; risk management; and monitoring of transactions
Risk Management and Monitoring of Transactions

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 9.3.3 of the workbook, the written AML procedures adopted by a registered intermediary must include: (a) policy for acceptance of clients; (b) procedure for identifying clients; (c) risk management; and (d) monitoring of transactions. The source describes these as the specified parameters, listed as four sub-items, and the correct option captures all of them. The Trap: Each single-parameter or two-parameter distractor is correct on its own, which makes them tempting. The AML written procedures, however, must cover all four parameters together to be compliant with the requirement. Note: Replaced the answer-randomization-fragile 'All of the above' wording with a standalone option that lists the four AML parameters, and removed the pro-tip line that was not source-grounded.
